info.title: Queek API Docs
info.description:
Build a store's website on its Queek catalogue: products, collections, promotions, reviews, pages and blog, plus a cart that hands off to Queek checkout. Read llms.txt on this host for the guide.

## Errors

Every error answers `{"error": {"code", "message", "field"?, "errors"?, "doc_url", "request_id"}}`.
Switch on `error.code`, never on the message. Codes: `ai_unavailable_in_test_mode`, `api_key_expired`, `api_key_mode_mismatch`, `api_key_revoked`, `app_embed_not_ready`, `app_grant_insufficient`, `app_handoff_failed`, `app_installation_gone`, `app_installation_pending`, `app_ip_not_allowed`, `app_proxy_failed`, `app_proxy_gone`, `app_token_revoked`, `bad_request`, `channel_gateway_unreachable`, `client_key_required`, `conflict`, `custom_domain_provisioning_failed`, `custom_gateway_forbidden`, `custom_gateway_kyc_required`, `custom_gateway_not_configured`, `custom_gateway_not_verified`, `custom_gateway_plan_required`, `custom_gateway_store_ineligible`, `custom_gateway_verification_failed`, `forbidden`, `gone`, `idempotency_key_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reuse`, `insufficient_scope`, `invalid_client`, `invalid_client_key`, `metafield_definition_missing`, `metafield_filter_unsupported_type`, `metafield_namespace_reserved`, `metafield_value_invalid`, `metaobject_definition_missing`, `metaobject_field_invalid`, `metaobject_reference_invalid`, `metaobject_type_reserved`, `method_not_allowed`, `not_found`, `origin_not_allowed`, `origin_required`, `payload_too_large`, `payment_amount_mismatch`, `plan_inactive`, `private_key_required`, `requires_slot`, `resync_cooldown`, `route_not_available`, `server_error`, `service_unavailable`, `subscription_feature_locked`, `too_many_requests`, `translation_digest_stale`, `translation_locale_is_default`, `translation_locale_is_primary`, `translation_locale_not_published`, `translation_max_published_locales`, `translation_unknown_key`, `translation_unknown_locale`, `unauthenticated`, `unknown_product_ref`, `unknown_service`, `unknown_variant_ref`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_failed`, `vendor_access_denied`, `vendor_mail_sender_forbidden`, `vendor_mail_sender_key_unavailable`, `vendor_mail_sender_not_configured`, `vendor_mail_sender_plan_required`, `vendor_mail_sender_verification_failed`.
Each error carries `doc_url` pointing at its own entry in the error reference, and `request_id` — always a
string — matching the `X-Request-Id` response header. Quote it in support.

## Legacy top-level keys

Additive only, never a second contract: on error bodies the runtime still emits the pre-contract
top-level keys shipped clients read. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on helper-produced refusals
(the shared controller and ApiError error helpers, plus the client-auth handler branches);
`request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies (storefront, client,
developer and dashboard surfaces) — the Merchant API reissues refusals, so there they live inside `error`.
They are documented separately under `QueekLegacyErrorKeys`, which no operation references. New integrations
switch on `error.*`.

## Request ids

Send `X-Request-Id` (8–128 chars matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$`) to correlate your trace with ours,
or read the one we generate — it is echoed on every response, error bodies included, and appears on every log line
of the request. `X-Queek-Api-Version` carries the API version (`v1`).

## Idempotency

Send `Idempotency-Key` on a write and a retry cannot execute twice. Same key + same body replays the stored
response verbatim with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` for 24h. Same key + a different body is
`409 idempotency_key_reuse`. A concurrent duplicate waits 15s for the first to finish, then replays;
past that it is `409 idempotency_key_in_progress`. Responses ≥ 400 are not stored, so a failure stays retryable.
The slot is vendor + caller + METHOD:path + key. The body is the fingerprint, not part of the slot. Operations that accept the header document it as a parameter.

## Rate limits

180 requests/min per API key + IP, or storefront origin + IP when no key is sent. On top of that, a private (`sk_live_`) key carries its
store's plan quota: `free` 60/min, `social_media` 120/min, `starter` 120/min, `growth` 240/min, `scale` 1200/min, `enterprise` 2400/min. sk_live_ private keys only. A pk_live_ public key is shared by every visitor of the store, so it gets no per-store bucket.
Exceeding either is `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`.

## Webhooks

Subscribe an endpoint per store and Queek posts the signed event to it. Topics are listed under `webhooks`
in this document; the body is signed with the Standard Webhooks scheme — HMAC-SHA256 over the base64-decoded secret, value `v1,<base64>` —
over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, tolerance 300s. A rotation keeps the previous secret valid for
24h and sends both signatures, space delimited. Delivery is 8 attempts on a published backoff;
an endpoint failing for 24h is disabled and the merchant notified.

`channel` is the messaging channel the order came through — never
the sales channel. The installed app source and caller reference
are exposed in the two keys below.

Import recognition: the sales channel that imported the order
(an app slug or legacy channel — null unless imported) and the
outside platform's own reference (null unless imported). Together with
`platform` (third_party) an app matches orders events to its
own records with no link table. Additive: both keys are null
for every order that is not an import.

Order attribution: the publication p_id the order was
imported through (null unless attributed). Readable by any
caller with order read scope — it discloses nothing new
beside custom_channel.

Vendor chain with the same unloaded-relation safety net as the
sibling order shapes: loaded relation first, then the
cache-backed lookup — never the silent platform default.

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties (jsonb, array-cast). Absent lines
render an empty object, never null — apps always see the key.
An app's single-use keys (claims, manage links) reach only the
app that issued them, never another app or key.

anyOf.description:
The receiver's own fields coming back to them: typed metafields the
merchant defined, and the opaque metadata an integrator wrote. This
is the whole point of order extensions — a webhook that omits the
ERP id forces the receiver to make a second call to match the order
to their own record.

transactions.description: Present only when the caller has merchant-orders-read; webhook deliveries include these fields only for an active app installation granted that scope.

refunds.description: Present only when the caller has merchant-orders-read; webhook deliveries include these fields only for an active app installation granted that scope. Only recorded Queek wallet refunds are included.

properties.description:
Per-line checkout properties. Always present as an object so
dashboard chips and the shopper page never branch on absence.
Bearer keys are withheld here too (dashboard, shopper page,
rider): the order email is their only carrier.

original.description:
Full original for hero-scale surfaces (featured/promo blocks render
~1100-1320 physical px — the 480px card upscales blurry there).

image_variants.description:
Sized variants of the primary image (thumbnail, card, hero),
keyed by size. Null when the image is a plain URL instead of an
uploaded image, or when no sized variants exist for it; the
other image keys are always present.

metafields.description:
Vendor-defined typed fields, keyed `namespace.key`. `{}` for a store
that has defined none, which costs no query (MetafieldPresenter).
Free-form `metadata` is deliberately NOT here: it is an
integrator's private bookkeeping and stays on the merchant API.
Client surface: draft entries and storefront-hidden definitions
are omitted from reference values (MetafieldPresenter).

checkout_url.description: Where to send the shopper: Queek's hosted checkout adopts this exact cart and completes address, delivery, payment and order confirmation. Present on a shopper's cart (the `X-Cart-Session` flow) for an API-key caller; absent otherwise.

rider_approved.description:
Whether this rider may actually open the storefront rider console —
is_rider alone is not enough, a vendor approval path must have
stamped rider_approved_at (see EnsureClientRider). The storefront
shows a "pending approval" state when is_rider && ! rider_approved.

image_variants.description:
Pre-sized copies of the image, resolved from its URL (categories
and collections store no media id).

Reserved namespaces (a store may not define in these): `queek`.
Owner types wired in this version: `product`, `order`.

content.description:

normalizer so a legacy/malformed section (e.g. a gallery with a
null slide) can never crash the storefront render. Same sanitizer
the write path uses, so serving == what a re-save would produce.

QueekLegacyErrorKeys.description: Additive legacy-compatibility top-level keys the runtime still emits on error bodies — never a replacement for `error.*`, which is the contract. `error_code` and `message` ride top-level on helper-produced refusals; `request_id` and `doc_url` ride top-level ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies (storefront, client, developer and dashboard surfaces) — merchant routes reissue refusals, so there they live inside `error` and the `X-Request-Id` header. Handler-produced bodies keep their own top-level keys with `error` stapled beside them. Not referenced by any operation response: new integrations switch on `error.code`.

error_code.description: Top-level mirror of `error.code` on helper-produced refusals (shared controller error helpers, client-auth handler branches).

message.description: Top-level mirror of `error.message` on the same helper-produced refusals as `error_code`.

request_id.description: Top-level mirror of `error.request_id` ONLY on non-reissued controller-helper bodies. Always a string when present.

doc_url.description: Top-level mirror of `error.doc_url`, same per-producer scope as top-level `request_id`: non-reissued controller-helper bodies only.

QueekStoreOtpChallenge.description: The challenge. The OTP itself travels out-of-band (SMS/WhatsApp/email); pass it to the matching `verify-otp` with the same identity.

phone.description: Echo of the identity the code was sent to.

user_exists.description: Whether this identity already has an account — `false` means call the register endpoint after verifying.

resend_in.description: Seconds until a new code may be requested.

debug_code.description: The code itself — returned outside production only, so automated tests can sign in without reading an inbox.

QueekStoreAuthSession.description: The customer session. Send `access_token` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; rotate with `POST auth/token/refresh` before `expires_at`.

token.description: Alias of `access_token`, kept for older clients.

is_new_user.description: Always true here — this endpoint creates the account.

QueekStoreNeedsRegistration.description: The code was right but this email has no account yet — finish with `POST auth/email/register-otp`, passing `verified_token`.

verified_token.description: Proof the email was just verified; the register call consumes it.

QueekStoreEmailVerifyResult.description: Either the customer session (existing account) or a registration ticket (new email).

QueekStorePostDetail.description: A store post (`QueekStorePage` shape) with its related posts.

QueekStoreSearchProduct.description: One product hit: the store product card (`QueekStoreProduct`, same final customer price as `products`) with presence meta stamped beside it — `distance`/`distance_text`/`delivery_fee` (also inside `shop`) stay null until the shopper shares a location.

distance.description: Kilometres to the vendor, 2dp; null without a shopper location.

delivery_fee.description: Delivery fee to the shopper (store currency); null when it cannot be computed.

QueekStoreSearch.description: Grouped matches over the store’s own published catalogue, newest-first. `type=all` (default) answers the first page of every section; a single `type` answers only that section — walk it with `starting_after`/`page` while its `has_more` is true.

sections.description: Only the requested section is present for a single-type search; all four for `type=all` (an empty section still answers `items: []`).

products.description: Product hits, same card and final customer price as `GET store/products`.

collections.description: Collection hits: id-title-slug stubs, never full cards.

pages.description: Page hits: id-title-slug stubs, never full cards.

posts.description: Post hits: id-title-slug stubs, never full cards.

QueekStoreAutocomplete.description: Instant suggestions over the store’s own catalogue: product hits, then collection hits, then query completions derived from the matched titles — at most 10 items.

price.description: Selling price (store currency); the full card carries `currency`.

QueekStoreCustomerAccount.description: The signed-in customer behind the bearer credential.

QueekStoreOrderPay.description: What the storefront needs to collect an online payment: the order totals plus both link forms. 422 when the order is not payable (not online, already paid, cancelled, rejected, refunded, or the link is unavailable).

QueekStoreFollowStatus.description: Follow state for this store. `shared_contact` rides on follow + status; unfollow answers without it.

shared_contact.description: Whether the customer shares contact details with this store.

QueekStoreWishlistItem.description: A saved wishlist row with the existing customer product card and optional self-contained variant details.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
